context_requirements: Expression of MTNR1A and/or MTNR1B on the target cell
An active melatonin/G-protein signaling tone for an antagonist to block
Assays performed at a time of day when endogenous melatonin signaling is engaged (not captured in this 6/24 h drug-treatment design)
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in the 978 landmark genes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines
A shared transcriptional signature across lines that is absent in vehicle controls and not attributable to vehicle or general toxicity
Evidence of MTNR1A/MTNR1B-dependent transcriptional modulation in these lines

evidence.supports: Luzindole, a melatonin receptor antagonist, was used to block melatonin effects in fish testis, indicating receptor-dependent action in vivo
Luzindole blocked electroacupuncture/melatonin-mediated reduction of NLRP3-pyroptosis in rat cerebral ischemia
Luzindole blocked melatonin-mediated Notch1/Hes1 antioxidant protection in diabetic aorta and VSMCs
Luzindole attenuated melatonin-induced apoptosis in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes, showing receptor dependence of melatonin's transcriptional/pro-apoptotic effects

changes: Removed PMID 33390989 from evidence: the abstract reports melatonin's effect on PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP signaling but does not test a melatonin receptor antagonist, so it does not support the antagonist mechanism.
